![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14193755/assets/dd3401de484cfd0cb096c812d3f7540c31373116ed21b32bc9856b96c4b2ada3.png)

The diagram shows a regular pentagon and a regular octagon. Find the measure of the shaded angle.
question.worked_solution:
The shaded angle is the sum of the measures of exterior angles of a regular pentagon and a regular octagon.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14193755/assets/cd6a3ba04cc8f3f301b6db6a825854ba260cd5ce5b0582b64431f80c78cb7771.png)

For any polygon, the exterior angles sum up to ${360}^{∘}.$ In a regular pentagon, there are $5$ equivalent exterior angles, so each has a measure of 

$$
\frac{{360}^{∘}}{5}={72}^{∘}.
$$

Likewise, in a regular octagon, there are $8$ equivalent exterior angles, so each has a measure of 

$$
\frac{{360}^{∘}}{8}={45}^{∘}.
$$

Therefore, the given angle has the following measure:

$$
{72}^{∘}+{45}^{∘}={117}^{∘}
$$
